Nerve injury is divided into 3 types, as follows: Neurapraxial injury occurs when a nerve is bruised or stunned but remains essentially intact. Axonotmesis describes a partial injury in which the axonal core of a nerve is damaged but the myelin sheath remains intact. These injuries usually regenerate at a rate of 1-3 mm per day. Neurotmesis is complete disruption of both axons and myelin sheath. It requires reapproximation of the nerve endings for healing to occur.
